title: TNM Downloader (The National Map) - USGS 3DEP elevation products
licence: US Government public domain. Wording seen: "All 3DEP products are public domain."
notes: OFF-LIST site. RESOLUTION: 3DEP publishes 1 m (lidar-derived, partial CONUS coverage), 1/3 arc-second (~10 m, stated on the data.gov 1/3 arc-second record) and 1 arc-second (~30 m). US territory only - no Scotland, so this is the route to a US glacial-valley stand-in, not to a literal glen. EXPORT: browser map application with an area-of-interest selector; no account, no login, no API key. CAVEAT ON 'CROP': the data.gov records describe these as tiled, pre-staged collections ('1/3rd arc-second DEM is available as pre-staged current and historical products tiled in GeoTIFF format'), i.e. you receive whole tiles and crop locally, rather than the server cutting your bounding box. For 1 m that means a large download for a 192 m world. FORMAT: GeoTIFF, stated as such on the data.gov collection records; migrated to Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF in 2020, which is still a GeoTIFF underneath. BIT DEPTH: not stated on any page I read - null, not guessed. VERIFICATION LIMIT: apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader is a JavaScript application; the fetch returned HTTP 200 and the page title 'TNM Downloader - The National Map' but no body text, so the URL and identity are verified and the in-app product list is not. The licence wording was therefore taken from the USGS collection record on data.gov and is linked in licence_seen_at rather than claimed from the app. Every www.usgs.gov page I tried returned an empty body to fetch, which is why no usgs.gov URL is cited here.

title: OpenTopography - USGS 1/3 arc-second Digital Elevation Model (10 m)
licence: Use License field on the dataset metadata page reads verbatim: "US Government Public Domain"
notes: OFF-LIST site. Best licence-plus-export combination found. RESOLUTION: page states '10 meter'. US only. EXPORT: true server-side bounding-box crop - the raster page carries a 'Select area of data to process' map plus manual Xmin/Ymin/Xmax/Ymax entry, and returns only the requested extent, so no desktop GIS is needed and the download is sized to the area. ACCOUNT: the raster page showed no academic-access banner (unlike the 1 m page, which showed one) and offers guest download; 'Advanced processing services are available to registered users'. FORMAT: the page lists Arc ASCII Grid, GeoTiff and IMG, plus optional KMZ visualisation. No PNG and no EXR option is offered, so a GeoTIFF-to-heightmap conversion is a step the Doer inherits. BIT DEPTH: not stated on the page. CITATION: page states users should acknowledge OpenTopography and the dataset source; DOI https://doi.org/10.5069/G98K778D. Report that alongside the public-domain wording and let the user decide - I am not judging whether an acknowledgement request and a public-domain licence conflict.

title: OpenTopography - USGS 1 meter Digital Elevation Model
licence: Use License field on the dataset metadata page reads verbatim: "US Government Public Domain". The raster page separately states "All 3DEP products are public domain."
notes: OFF-LIST site. HARD ACCESS GATE - read before ranking this above anything. The raster download page states access is currently limited to US academic users with '.edu addresses' who must log in, plus K-12 teachers, international academics and informal educators by application, or OpenTopography+ members. If the user has no .edu address this candidate is unusable and candidate 1 or 2 is the route. RESOLUTION: 1 m, lidar-derived, US only. At 1 m/px a 192 m world maps 1:1 to a 192x192 px crop, which is the only source here that does that without upsampling. EXPORT: same server-side bounding-box crop as the 10 m dataset ('Select area of data to process' map). FORMATS: the raster page did not itself list output formats; Arc ASCII Grid / GeoTiff / IMG are what the sibling OpenTopography raster pages offer, so treat the format list here as inferred from sibling pages, not read off this one. BIT DEPTH: not stated. DISCREPANCY WORTH KNOWING: the data.gov mirror record for this same OpenTopography dataset (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/usgs-1-meter-digital-elevation-model) carries a License field of https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 while its own body text says 'All 3DEP products are public domain'. Two different licence claims for one dataset on two pages. Stated, not resolved.

title: OpenTopography - NASADEM Global Digital Elevation Model (30 m)
licence: OpenTopography's own Use License field reads verbatim: "Not Provided". The underlying NASA product page states the data is "openly shared, without restriction, in accordance with the EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance".
notes: OFF-LIST site. The only shortlisted route that covers Scotland. RESOLUTION: page states '30 meter'. At 30 m/px a 192 m world is about 6x6 samples - too coarse to carry a valley silhouette 1:1. It is usable if the plan is to crop a LARGER real glen (say 2 km across, ~67x67 px) and compress it into the 192 m footprint; that is a decision for the user, not an assumption I have made. EXPORT: server-side bounding-box crop with a map selector and manual Xmin/Ymin/Xmax/Ymax entry; guest download available without an account. FORMAT: Arc ASCII Grid, GeoTiff, IMG, plus optional KMZ. BIT DEPTH: not stated. LICENCE CAUTION: OpenTopography prints 'Use License: Not Provided' for this dataset on both the raster page and the metadata page (https://portal.opentopography.org/datasetMetadata?otCollectionID=OT.032021.4326.2) - the licence in the licence field above therefore comes from NASA's own catalogue entry for the source product, NOT from the redistributor. OpenTopography does print a citation and an acknowledgement string (NASA JPL, NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second V001, DOI https://doi.org/10.5069/G93T9FD9). The sibling SRTM GL1 30 m dataset (https://portal.opentopography.org/raster?opentopoID=OTSRTM.082015.4326.1) is the same shape in every respect and also reads 'Use License: Not Provided'; NASADEM is listed here rather than SRTM GL1 only because its NASA source page carries the clearer restriction wording.

title: NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second V001 (NASA LP DAAC)
licence: Page states the dataset is "openly shared, without restriction, in accordance with the EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance".
notes: OFF-LIST site. This is the canonical NASA source for NASADEM and the clearest licence wording of anything read on this run - it is listed for that reason, not because it is the easiest download. RESOLUTION: page states '30 Meters x 30 Meters'. Global. EXPORT: NO bounded crop. Distribution is whole 1-degree granules through Earthdata Search / LP DAAC, so cropping to a 192 m footprint is a local step. ACCOUNT: an Earthdata Login is required for LP DAAC distribution; the page links Earthdata Login in its resources but does not state the requirement in so many words, so treat 'login required' as strongly indicated rather than quoted. FORMAT: HGT, also available as NetCDF4. No GeoTIFF offered on this product. BIT DEPTH: not stated on the page - do not assume, even though HGT is conventionally a raw integer grid. CITATION: DOI https://doi.org/10.5067/MEASURES/NASADEM/NASADEM_HGT.001.
